nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
﴿خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَها﴾: (تَرَوْنَها) may be in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a naʿt (adjective) of عمد, i.e. "without visible pillars"; and it may be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū Jaʿfar said:
And I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: it is preferable that it be resumptive, so that the statement is complete at بغير عمد. ﴿أَنْ تَمِيدَ﴾ is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "out of aversion lest it sway"; the Kufans take it in the sense of "so that it does not sway" (لئلا تميد).
﴿فَأَنْبَتْنا فِيها مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾: from Ibn ʿAbbās: "of every fine kind". Al-Shaʿbī interpreted it as referring to people, because they are created from the earth; he said: whoever of them goes to Paradise is the noble (al-karīm), and whoever goes to the Fire is the base (al-laʾīm). Someone else interpreted it to mean that the sperm-drop is created from dust, and the apparent sense of the Qur'an indicates this.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
﴿هذا خَلْقُ اللَّهِ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). ﴿فَأَرُونِي ماذا خَلَقَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾: «ما» is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is «ذا», ذا being in the sense of الذي ("which"); on this view خلق acts on an omitted hāʾ. [Accordingly] you say: ماذا تعلّمت أنحوٌ أم شعرٌ ("What is it that you learned, grammar or poetry?", in the nominative). And «ما» may be in the position of the accusative governed by خلق, with «ذا» redundant (zāʾida); on this view you say: ماذا تعلمت أنحواً أم شعراً (in the accusative). ﴿بَلِ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾: nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ is in the position of the khabar.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا لُقْمانَ الْحِكْمَةَ أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ وَمَنْ يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّما يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ كَفَرَ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ حَمِيدٌ﴾ (12) ﴿وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنا لُقْمانَ الْحِكْمَةَ﴾: two objects. لقمان is a diptote (it does not take tanwīn) because at its end are an added alif and nūn, so it resembles the pattern فَعْلان whose feminine is فَعْلى; it is not declined as a triptote when definite because that is a second heaviness, and it is declined as a triptote when indefinite because one of the two heavinesses has gone. ʿIkrima claimed that Luqmān was a prophet, and in the ḥadīth it is stated that he was an Abyssinian. ﴿أَنِ اشْكُرْ لِلَّهِ﴾ admits two analyses: one is that «أن» is in the sense of أي, explicative (mufassira), i.e. "We said to him: Give thanks"; the other is that it is in the position of the accusative with the verb included in its ṣila, as Sībawayh related: كتبت إليه أن قم ("I wrote to him that he should stand"), except that this view is far-fetched. ﴿وَمَنْ يَشْكُرْ فَإِنَّما يَشْكُرُ لِنَفْسِهِ﴾: [يشكر is] jussive (majzūm) by the condition; the nominative is also permissible, taking مَن in the sense of الذي ("he who").

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿وَإِذْ قالَ لُقْمانُ لِابْنِهِ وَهُوَ يَعِظُهُ﴾: «إذ» is in the position of the accusative, the meaning being "And remember". Abū Isḥāq related in his book on the Qur'an that «إذ» is in the position of the accusative governed by آياتنا [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps آتينا is meant, in light of what follows], and that the meaning is: "And We certainly gave Luqmān wisdom when he said". Abū Jaʿfar said: I reckon this a mistake, because there is a wāw in the passage that prevents it, and moreover the name Luqmān is mentioned after قال. ﴿يا بُنَيَّ﴾ is with kasra on the yāʾ [i.e. يا بُنَيِّ], because it points to the omitted yāʾ [of the first person]; whoever reads it with fatḥa does so, in his view, because of the lightness of the fatḥa.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t:
﴿إِنَّها﴾: an allusion to the story (al-qiṣṣa) or to the deed (al-fiʿla), or in the sense of: "The thing you asked me about…", because it is related that he asked him. The Basrans permit إنّها زيدٌ ضربته ("It is [the case that] Zayd, I struck him"), in the sense of "the story is…", while the Kufans permit this only with a feminine. ﴿إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ مِنْ خَرْدَلٍ﴾: (مِثْقالَ) is the khabar of «تك», whose noun is latent (muḍmar) in it. Abū Ḥātim considered it unlikely that one should read ﴿إِنْ تَكُ مِثْقالَ حَبَّةٍ﴾ with the nominative [i.e. مِثْقالُ], because مثقال is masculine, so in his view it is only permissible with yāʾ [i.e. إن يكُ]. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is permissible and sound; it is construed according to the meaning, because the meaning is the same. This is frequent in the speech of the Arabs; one says اجتمعت أهلُ اليمامة ("the people of al-Yamāma gathered", with a feminine verb), because one of their expressions is اجتمعت اليمامة. [Translator's note: the text reads أهل القيامة, which appears to be a misprint for أهل اليمامة, as the following words show.] Al-Farrāʾ claimed that analogous to the verse is the poet's saying:
339-
وتشرق بالقول الّذي قد أذعته ... كما شرقت صدر القناة من الدّم
(You choke on the word you have spread abroad, as the upper part of the spear-shaft is choked with blood.)
As for ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ﴾, it is parenthetical within Luqmān's speech, as Shuʿba related from Simāk ibn Ḥarb from Muṣʿab ibn Saʿd from his father, who said: Saʿd's mother said to Saʿd: "Has Allah, Majestic and Mighty, not commanded dutifulness to one's mother? By Allah, I will neither eat nor drink until you disbelieve in Muḥammad ﷺ." When they wanted to feed her, they would prise open her mouth with a stick and pour the food and drink into it. Then there was revealed ﴿وَوَصَّيْنَا الْإِنْسانَ بِوالِدَيْهِ﴾ up to ﴿وَإِنْ جاهَداكَ عَلى أَنْ تُشْرِكَ بِي ما لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِ عِلْمٌ﴾, the verse. As for the accusative of «وهنا على وهن», Abū Jaʿfar said: I do not know of any of the grammarians who has mentioned it; it would be a second object with the preposition omitted, i.e. "she carried him with weakness upon weakness", or "and she increased in weakness upon weakness". ﴿مَعْرُوفاً﴾ is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun). Abū Isḥāq claimed in his book that «أن» is in the position of the accusative and that the meaning is: "And We enjoined upon man concerning his parents that he give thanks to Me and to his parents." This view is far-fetched according to the school of Sībawayh, and as far as I know Abū Isḥāq mentioned nothing else. Better than it is that «أن» be explicative (mufassira), the meaning being: "We said to him: Give thanks to Me and to your parents."

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿يا بُنَيَّ أَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ﴾: the meaning of establishing the prayer is completing it with all its obligatory elements, as one says: فلان قيّم بعمله الذي وليه ("So-and-so is upright in the work he was put in charge of"), i.e. he has given the work all its dues; from this is: هذا قوام الأمر ("this is the mainstay of the matter"). ﴿وَاصْبِرْ عَلى ما أَصابَكَ﴾: that is, that he not be driven by anxiety into disobedience to Allah; and likewise patience in refraining from sins.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿وَلا تُصَعِّرْ خَدَّكَ لِلنَّاسِ﴾: we have already mentioned it. It is reported from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd that he said: «تصاعر» is [an action] from one party, like عافاه الله ("Allah granted him well-being"). ﴿وَلا تَمْشِ فِي الْأَرْضِ مَرَحاً﴾: i.e. strutting and arrogant. It is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:19-19.t:
﴿وَاقْصِدْ فِي مَشْيِكَ﴾: i.e. be moderate, and moderation is the most praiseworthy of things; and likewise ﴿وَاغْضُضْ مِنْ صَوْتِكَ﴾: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, disciplined him by commanding him to give up shouting in people's faces out of contempt for them. ﴿إِنَّ أَنْكَرَ الْأَصْواتِ لَصَوْتُ الْحَمِيرِ﴾: Abū ʿUbayda said: i.e. the harshest; and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said [the same]; both of them [take it] as figurative.
And in the ḥadīth: "No donkey brays and no dog barks except that it sees a devil."

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ﴾: (مَنْ) is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), or by virtue of the adjectival qualification.
It is reported from two of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that «لهو الحديث» here means singing, and that it is forbidden by the Book and the Sunna. The implied meaning is then: "And among the people is he who buys one possessed of amusement (ذا لهو)" or "one (feminine) possessed of amusement (ذات لهو)", like ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾ [Yūsuf: 82]; or the implied meaning is: since he only buys her and goes to extremes in her price, it is as though he bought the amusement itself. ﴿لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ means: in order to lead others astray; and whoever read it ليضل [Translator's note: i.e. لِيَضِلَّ, "in order to go astray"] takes it as what necessarily follows for him in his view. ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَها﴾ is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim; al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ﴿وَيَتَّخِذَها﴾, conjoined to ليضلّ. [Translator's note: the vowelling of the two readings has been lost in the printed text; the context shows the first group read وَيَتَّخِذُها with the nominative and the second وَيَتَّخِذَها with the accusative, conjoined to لِيُضِلَّ.] The nominative is from two angles: one is that it is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to يشتري, and the other is that it is resumptive (mustaʾnaf). The hāʾ is an allusion to the verses (āyāt), and it may be an allusion to the path (al-sabīl), because al-sabīl is treated as both masculine and feminine.

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿كَأَنَّ فِي أُذُنَيْهِ وَقْراً﴾: (وَقْراً) is the noun (ism) of kaʾanna. The ḍamma [in أُذُن] may be dropped because of its heaviness, so one says: أُذْن.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
﴿أَلَمْ تَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُمْ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظاهِرَةً وَباطِنَةً وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلا هُدىً وَلا كِتابٍ مُنِيرٍ﴾ (20) ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَوْا أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُمْ ما فِي السَّماواتِ وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: this is among the favours of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, to the children of Adam, for all things are made subservient to them: sun, moon, stars, and angels who surround them and bring them their benefits; and sky, and what is in both, which cannot be counted. ﴿وَأَسْبَغَ عَلَيْكُمْ نِعَمَهُ ظاهِرَةً وَباطِنَةً﴾: [ظاهرة and باطنة are accusative] as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Whoever read نعمةً ظاهرةً وباطنةً made it a naʿt (adjective); this is the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, transmitted by sound chains, and he explained it as: Islam. The explanation of this is that Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said regarding His saying, Majestic and Mighty:
﴿وَلكِنْ يُرِيدُ لِيُطَهِّرَكُمْ وَلِيُتِمَّ نِعْمَتَهُ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 6]: he said: [it means] He will admit you into Paradise; and the completion of Allah's favour upon the servant is that He admits him into Paradise. Likewise, since the outcome of Islam is Paradise, it was called a favour (niʿma). And from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said [about] ﴿وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾: he said: he is al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿أَوَلَوْ كانَ الشَّيْطانُ يَدْعُوهُمْ إِلى عَذابِ السَّعِيرِ﴾: i.e. "Even if it were so, would they follow him?", by way of rebuke.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَنْ يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾: the reading of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī is ﴿وَمَنْ يُسْلِمْ وَجْهَهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ﴾. [Translator's note: the vowelling of al-Sulamī's variant has been lost in the printed text; from what follows it is evidently يُسَلِّمْ.] He said: «يسلم» is better known in this [usage], as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَقُلْ أَسْلَمْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّهِ﴾. The meaning of «أسلمت وجهي لله» is: I directed my worship to Allah and affirmed that there is no god other than Him. It may also be that the implied meaning is: "whoever surrenders himself to Allah", like ﴿كُلُّ شَيْءٍ هالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُ﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 88], whose meaning is "except Him". And يسلّم would be for intensification (al-taktīr), except that the usage of سلّمت is in the sense of "I handed over"; one says سلّمت في الحنطة ("I paid in advance for wheat"), and one may also say أسلمت. Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَقَدِ اسْتَمْسَكَ بِالْعُرْوَةِ الْوُثْقى﴾: he said: [it is] "There is no god but Allah".

nahhas-irab:27-27.t:
﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّما فِي الْأَرْضِ مِنْ شَجَرَةٍ أَقْلامٌ﴾: «أنّ» is in the position of the nominative, the implied meaning being "and if this were to happen", and «أقلام» is the khabar (predicate) of أنّ. ﴿وَالْبَحْرُ يَمُدُّهُ﴾: [البحرُ is] nominative from two angles: one is conjunction to the position [of أنّ and its noun], and the other is that it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿وَالْبَحْرَ يَمُدُّهُ﴾ with the accusative, by conjunction to the wording [i.e. to ما, the noun of أنّ]. [Translator's note: the printed text here shows the nominative vowelling in the Qur'anic quotation; the accusative is meant.] Yūnus related from Ibn Abī ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ [Translator's note: so in the text; probably Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ is meant] that he said: "I know no justification for the nominative unless the sea is made [into] pens." Abū ʿUbayd prefers the nominative because of the large number who read it so, except that he said: whoever reads with the nominative is obliged to read ﴿وكَتَبْنا عَلَيْهِمْ فِيها أَنَّ النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ وَالْعَيْنَ بِالْعَيْنِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 45] [with the nominative, وَالْعَيْنُ]. Abū Jaʿfar said:
This differs from that according to Sībawayh. Sībawayh said: i.e. "while the sea is in such a state"; he makes the wāw convey the ḥāl, and this is not [the case] in ﴿وَالْعَيْنَ بِالْعَيْنِ﴾. (يمدّه): «يُمِدُّه» is also related, on the basis that the two are two dialects with one meaning; and a distinction between the two dialects is also related: that for what increases something one says مدّه يمدّه, as you say مدّ النيلُ الخليجَ ("the Nile swelled the canal"), i.e. increased it, and أمدّ الله جلّ وعزّ الخليجَ بالنيل ("Allah, Majestic and Mighty, supplied the canal with the Nile"). This is the better of the two views, and it is the school of al-Farrāʾ. تمدّه is also permissible. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِ سَبْعَةُ أَبْحُرٍ﴾: with the feminine form of سبعة. ﴿ما نَفِدَتْ كَلِماتُ اللَّهِ﴾: Qatāda said: They said: "What Muḥammad ﷺ has brought will run out," so Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed this.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
﴿ما خَلْقُكُمْ وَلا بَعْثُكُمْ إِلَّا كَنَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ﴾: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: i.e. the initial creation of all of you is only like the creation of a single soul, and your resurrection on the Day of Resurrection is only like the resurrection of a single soul. Abū Jaʿfar said:
And thus the grammarians interpreted it, in the sense of "only like the creation of a single soul", like ﴿وَسْئَلِ الْقَرْيَةَ﴾.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: ﴿يُولِجُ اللَّيْلَ فِي النَّهارِ وَيُولِجُ النَّهارَ فِي اللَّيْلِ﴾: from Ibn Masʿūd, who said: the shortness of the winter day within the length of its night, and the shortness of the summer night within the length of its day.

nahhas-irab:32-32.t: ﴿وَإِذا غَشِيَهُمْ مَوْجٌ كَالظُّلَلِ﴾: because the way of waves, when they become violent, is to rise high. Al-Farrāʾ said: by الظّلل He means the clouds. Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, may Allah have mercy on them, said regarding قاضٍ and جازٍ: one pauses on them without tāʾ [Translator's note: so in the text; probably "without yāʾ" (بغير ياء) is meant, as the following shows], and their reason for that is so that it be known that in continuous speech it is likewise. The analogy would have been to pause on them with the yāʾ, because the tanwīn disappears in pause. Yūnus related that some Arabs whose language is trusted pause with the yāʾ, saying: جاءني قاضي وجازي.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ﴾: al-Farrāʾ claimed that there is a sense of negation in this, i.e. no one knows it except Allah, Majestic and Mighty. Abū Jaʿfar said: The sense of negation and affirmation came to be in it only through the Messenger ﷺ having specified that, because he ﷺ [explained] regarding the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty, ﴿وَعِنْدَهُ مَفاتِحُ الْغَيْبِ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 59] ﴿لا يَعْلَمُها إِلَّا هُوَ﴾ that they are these. Abū Isḥāq said: whoever claims that he knows anything of this has disbelieved: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ الْغَيْثَ وَيَعْلَمُ ما فِي الْأَرْحامِ وَما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ ماذا تَكْسِبُ غَداً وَما تَدْرِي نَفْسٌ بِأَيِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾. Some Arabs say: بأيّة أرض. Whoever says بأيّ أرض says: the feminine of الأرض suffices for the feminine of أيّ; and whoever says بأيّة أرض says: أيّ can stand alone, coming without iḍāfa (being made a muḍāf); if someone said جاءتني امرأة ("a woman came to me"), you would say: أيّة ("which one?"). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾: [خبير is] a naʿt (adjective) of عليم, or a khabar (predicate) after a khabar.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t: (الم تِلْكَ) is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), that is: "these are those". One also says تيك. (آياتُ الْكِتابِ الْحَكِيمِ) is a badal (substitute) for «تلك».

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: (هُدىً وَرَحْمَةً) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), like (هذِهِ ناقَةُ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ آيَةً) [al-Aʿrāf: 73, and Hūd: 64]. This is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī. Ḥamza read هدى ورحمةٌ in the nominative, which is on one of two bases: one is on an implied mubtadaʾ, because it is the beginning of a verse; the other is that it is the khabar (predicate) of تلك.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: (الَّذِينَ يُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ) is in the position of the nominative on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ, because it is the beginning of a verse; or in the position of the accusative in the sense of "I mean"; or in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) for (المحسنين).
